notice: Fictional tabletop discussion prompts only; no real customer, tenant, or incident data.

scenarios.title: Unexpected privileged sign-in
scenarios.context: A fictional customer reports an unfamiliar sign-in alert for an administrator account. The alert alone does not establish account compromise.
discussion_prompts: Who owns incident command, identity investigation, and customer communication?
Which logs and timestamps should be preserved in the approved evidence store?
What corroborating signals distinguish travel, automation, token theft, and false positive?
Which containment actions require customer authorization, and who can approve them?
How will access restoration and session revocation be verified?
safety_constraints: Do not use real identities or credentials
Do not execute containment actions in this exercise

scenarios.title: Device enrollment service degradation
scenarios.context: A fictional staged device deployment shows increased enrollment failures after a configuration change; impact scope and causal link are initially uncertain.
discussion_prompts: How will the team establish affected cohorts and compare against a baseline?
What is the safe decision point for pausing the next rollout ring?
Who owns rollback approval, and what dependencies could make rollback unsafe?
Which signals verify recovery without weakening security controls?
How should the MSP communicate uncertainty, workaround, and next update time?
safety_constraints: Do not disable security controls broadly
